instructions:
Notices:

Notice to Massachusetts Applicants:  It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment.  An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.


Colorado Residents: In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.


Notice to Georgia applicants:  The use of tobacco, e-cigarettes, vape products, and other nicotine ingestion methods is prohibited in all work areas, except in specially designated outdoor locations.  


Notice to Maryland Applicants:  Under Maryland law, an employer may not require or demand, as a condition of employment, prospective employment, or continued employment, that an individual submit to or take a lie detector or similar test.  An employer who violates this law is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine not exceeding $100.


Notice to San Francisco Residents:  Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.


Immigration Sponsorship is not available for this role.  Procter & Gamble does not sponsor candidates for non-immigrant visas or permanent residency except in some areas that in P&G’s sole discretion require highly specialized backgrounds. 

 

It is important to answer the following questions accurately.  Failure to provide an accurate answer may be grounds for revoking an offer of employment or termination of employment in the future.

 

For more information related to the question below, click HERE.

questions.body: Are you authorized to work in the US?

branchingQuestion.body: Please select the statement that best applies to you.

possibleAnswers.answerText: Yes, I have work authorization that has no restrictions (applicable to US citizens or nationals, lawful permanent residents, asylees and refugees).
Yes, but my work authorization requires either school approval (CPT or OPT) or employer-supported USCIS approval (meaning TN, H-1B, H-1B1, E-3, OPT, STEM OPT, among others).

Yes, I have current work authorization that does not require employer sponsorship, but my authorization is subject to renewal or extension (e.g., DACA, TPS, DED, VAWA, U or T visa, etc.). This selection does not apply if you have OPT or STEM OPT.
No, I am not authorized to work in the US currently and would need school approval or employer-supported USCIS approval to begin work.
